timeline.event: ACCC commenced informal review under the Informal Merger Review Process Guidelines.
Former provisional date for announcement of findings (13 November 2025) brought forward to 24 October 2025. ACCC announced it would not oppose the proposed acquisition.

body_sections.Summary: Cuscal Limited ( Cuscal ) proposes to acquire 100% of the issued share capital in Indue Limited ( Indue ). Cuscal is an ASX-listed company (ASX: CCL), which supplies end-to-end payment facilitation services in Australia. Cuscal is also an authorised deposit-taking institution ( ADI ). Indue is a payment facilitation company operating in Australia, and is also an ADI. Indue supplies certain payment facilitation services and aggregates certain third-party payment facilitation services. Cuscal and Indue overlap in the provision of account-to-account payment facilitation services (including switching and messaging through NPP, BECS and BPay and ESA settlement) and card issuing payment facilitation services (including credit, debit and prepaid card processing, BIN sponsorship, card switching, card management services and digital card provisioning). Cuscal and Indue also offer non-payment specific services such as fraud mitigation services. Cuscal also provides merchant acquiring, card and ATM switching. They also provide consumer data right ( CDR ) services. Indue does not overlap with Cuscal in the supply of these forms of payment facilitation services.
body_sections.Market definition: The ACCC considered the likely impact of the Proposed Acquisition on competition in market(s) for payment facilitation services used by small and mutual bank customers and other customers. For the purposes of this assessment, the ACCC did not need to reach a concluded view on the boundaries of the relevant markets.
body_sections.Competition analysis: The ACCC concluded that the proposed acquisition is not likely to substantially lessen competition in any market in Australia The ACCC found that Cuscal and Indue are two of the larger suppliers of payment facilitation services, particularly to small and mutual bank customers. However, the ACCC found that many customers source their payment facilitation requirements from multiple suppliers. The ACCC also considered the impact of broader industry trends on competition. In particular, there has been significant consolidation among small and mutual banks in recent years and this is likely to continue. This will limit the number of core banking customers Cuscal, Indue, and other payment facilitation suppliers can compete for. Digitisation in payment facilitation services may also lower the cost of switching between service providers and reduce barriers to entry. The ACCC also had regard to the views of market participants. Many of the small and mutual banks that acquire payment facilitation services from the merger parties considered that the proposed acquisition would achieve efficiencies and improve capacity to invest in enhanced services.
